xBRIEFInfo.description: Spike: starred photo does not persist

plan.title: SPIKE: starring a gallery photo does not change the profile photo after first save

narratives.Overview: On first creation of a gallery, starring any photo sets the profile picture. After the gallery has been saved once, starring a different photo no longer changes it. Photos added later do not respect the change either.
narratives.Problem:
What is verified: the star is a direct assignment (EntityProfileEditorView.swift:236) - `photoUrl = url`, with `photoUrl == url` driving the filled/unfilled state. The control writes the right variable, so the failure is DOWNSTREAM of the tap: in save, in the download/token rewrite, or in what is re-read on reopen.

Root cause is NOT established.
narratives.Action:
SPIKE FIRST. Reproduce the failure and identify the actual mechanism before writing any fix.

A plausible mechanism - explicitly a hypothesis, not a diagnosis - is the local-token scheme: after the first save, photos are downloaded into the library and galleryUrls may hold local tokens rather than original URLs, so `photoUrl == url` no longer compares the same strings. preserveLocalPrimaryIfBeingReplaced (:704) is guarded by `(initialProfile?.photoUrl ?? "").isEmpty` - it runs ONLY when there was no primary before, which is suspiciously close to 'works the first time, not after'.
narratives.Constraint: Two performance findings in this project were wrong when investigated, and each cost a wasted fix. Do not treat the hypothesis above as the diagnosis.
narratives.Risk: The previous primary must not be lost when replaced. A local-only primary with no source URL is unrecoverable once overwritten.
narratives.Test:
T3 - starring changes the profile photo on a brand-new gallery, on a saved gallery, and on a gallery with photos added since. The middle case is the reported failure.
T4 - replacing a local-only primary preserves the old file.
narratives.Source: Spec R4. Code: EntityProfileEditorView.swift:236, :704. Related but distinct from issue #13 (tapping a thumbnail opens the wrong photo).

items.title: Reproduce the failure on a saved gallery
Identify the actual mechanism - do not assume the token hypothesis
Implement the fix with T3 and T4
